items.title: James Moody interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998
items.q: So Gus Aphalia — this is the truth — the arranger, he went into the john and jotted down the harmonies

ctx.x: So up until that point, even when you recorded “Moody’s Mood for Love,” it was all coming from your ear.

All by ear. “Moody’s Mood for Love,” the same thing. What I did was, I was playing tenor, so Lars Gullin, who was a very fantastic baritone jazz player in Sweden — good musicians in Sweden boy, wonderful — he had this beat up looking silver alto sitting by him at the record date. I asked him do you mind if I look at it? He said no. In the old days it was different. You played other people’s horns. You know you would never do that now.
